question: My property policy says Special Form. What does that actually cover, and what is carved out?
aliases: causes of loss special form CP 10 30 explained
does commercial property cover flood or earthquake
ensuing loss exception fire following earthquake
shortAnswer: Special Form inverts the usual question. Where Special is shown in the Declarations, Covered Causes of Loss means direct physical loss unless the loss is excluded or limited in the policy [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. So the perils are not listed; the exclusions are, and section B.1 lists eight: Ordinance Or Law, Earth Movement, Governmental Action, Nuclear Hazard, Utility Services, War And Military Action, Water, and Fungus, Wet Rot, Dry Rot And Bacteria [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. The sentence that decides most disputed claims is the one introducing them.
assumes: The Declarations show Special rather than Basic or Broad, since that is what brings this form into play [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
You are reading the 09 17 edition of the form [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Editions differ and endorsements amend exclusions, so the policy issued governs.
You are asking what the form excludes, not whether a particular loss falls inside an exclusion, which is decided on the facts.
why:
The lead-in to the B.1 exclusions is doing more work than the exclusions themselves. It states that the insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused directly or indirectly by any of the listed causes, and that such loss or damage is excluded regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence to the loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Directly or indirectly, concurrently or in any sequence. That is an anti-concurrent-causation clause, and its effect is that a covered peril mixing with an excluded one does not rescue the claim. A further sentence adds that these exclusions apply whether or not the loss event results in widespread damage or affects a substantial area [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17], so scale is not an argument either.

Against that, the exceptions matter enormously, because they are the only way back in.

Earth Movement covers earthquake including tremors and aftershocks with related sinking, rising or shifting; landslide with the same; mine subsidence meaning subsidence of a man-made mine; earth sinking other than sinkhole collapse, rising or shifting, including soil conditions causing settling, cracking or other disarrangement of foundations; and separately volcanic eruption, explosion or effusion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. It applies whether any of those is caused by an act of nature or is otherwise caused [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. But if earth movement in the first four branches results in fire or explosion, the insurer pays for the loss caused by that fire or explosion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Fire following earthquake is covered; the earthquake damage is not. And volcanic eruption has its own exception for resulting fire, building glass breakage or Volcanic Action, with Volcanic Action defined in the exclusion itself as loss from airborne volcanic blast or shock waves, ash, dust or particulate matter, or lava flow, all eruptions within any 168-hour period counting as one occurrence, and expressly not including the cost to remove ash that has not caused direct physical loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Water is the exclusion most often misread as meaning flood. It reaches flood, surface water, waves including tidal wave and tsunami, tides, tidal water, overflow of any body of water, or spray from any of these, whether or not driven by wind including storm surge; mudslide or mudflow; water that backs up or overflows or is discharged from a sewer, drain, sump, sump pump or related equipment; water under the ground surface pressing on or flowing or seeping through foundations, walls, floors, paved surfaces, basements, doors, windows or other openings; and waterborne material carried by any of that [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Sewer backup and groundwater seepage are in the same exclusion as the ocean. It applies regardless of whether any of it is an act of nature, and gives failure of a dam, levee or seawall as an example [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Its exception: if any of those results in fire, explosion or sprinkler leakage, the insurer pays for the loss caused by that, with the qualifier that sprinkler leakage must itself be a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Ordinance Or Law excludes enforcement of or compliance with any ordinance regulating construction, use or repair, or requiring the tearing down of property including debris removal, and applies both where an ordinance is enforced even though the property has not been damaged and where increased costs are incurred to comply in the course of construction, repair, renovation, remodeling or demolition following a physical loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. That is why code-upgrade cover is bought separately.

Utility Services excludes failure of power, communication, water or other utility supplied to the premises, however caused, where the failure originates away from the premises or originates at the premises but involves equipment supplying the service from an off-site source, and also a power surge that would not have occurred but for such a failure, with an exception where the failure or surge results in a Covered Cause of Loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Failure includes lack of sufficient capacity and reduction in supply, and communication services include Internet access and electronic, cellular or satellite network access [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Two more carry exceptions. Governmental Action excludes seizure or destruction by order of governmental authority, but pays for acts of destruction ordered at the time of a fire to prevent its spread, if the fire would be covered [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Nuclear Hazard excludes nuclear reaction, radiation or radioactive contamination however caused, but pays for resulting fire [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. War And Military Action is the one exclusion in that group with no stated exception at all [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Fungus, wet rot, dry rot and bacteria are excluded as to presence, growth, proliferation, spread or any activity, with the insurer paying where they result in a specified cause of loss, and with the exclusion not applying where they result from fire or lightning, or to the extent the section E Additional Coverage responds [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. That Additional Coverage is narrow and capped: it applies only where the fungus or rot results from a specified cause of loss other than fire or lightning, or from flood where a Flood Coverage Endorsement applies, occurring during the policy period, and only if all reasonable means were used to save and preserve the property; it is limited to $15,000 for all such loss in a 12-month period and does not increase any Limit of Insurance [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Beyond section B.1 sit the wear-and-tear group and the conduct group. Paragraph B.2.d excludes wear and tear; rust, corrosion, decay, deterioration, hidden or latent defect or any quality in property causing it to damage itself; smog; settling, cracking, shrinking or expansion; nesting or infestation or discharge by insects, birds, rodents or other animals; mechanical breakdown including rupture by centrifugal force; and dampness or dryness of atmosphere, temperature extremes, and marring or scratching [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Each of those has a general way back: if one results in a specified cause of loss or building glass breakage, the insurer pays for that resulting loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17], and mechanical breakdown resulting in elevator collision is paid specifically [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Dishonesty is split in a way worth knowing. B.2.h excludes dishonest or criminal acts including theft by the named insured, partners, members, officers, managers, employees including temporary employees and leased workers, directors, trustees or authorised representatives, alone or in collusion, and separately theft by anyone to whom the insured entrusts the property [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. It applies whether or not during normal hours, and it does not apply to acts of destruction by employees or authorised representatives, though theft by those same people remains uncovered [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. An angry employee who smashes something is a different question from one who takes it.

And neglect of an insured to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property from further damage at and after the time of loss is excluded outright [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].

Section B.3 catches the design-and-decision group: weather conditions where they contribute in any way with a B.1 excluded cause; acts or decisions including failures to act or decide of any person, group, organisation or governmental body; and faulty, inadequate or defective planning, zoning, development, surveying, siting, design, specifications, workmanship, repair, construction, renovation, remodeling, grading, compaction, materials or maintenance [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Its exception is the ensuing-loss rule again: if one of those results in a Covered Cause of Loss, the insurer pays for that resulting loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
whatChanges: Whether an excluded cause contributed to the loss at all, since the exclusions apply directly or indirectly and regardless of anything contributing concurrently or in any sequence [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether the excluded cause produced a further covered peril, since several exclusions pay for the resulting fire, explosion or specified cause of loss [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether water came from a sewer, sump or the ground rather than a burst pipe, since backup and seepage sit inside the Water exclusion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether a utility failure originated off the premises or involved off-site supply equipment, which is the test in the exclusion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether increased cost is attributable to an ordinance, which is excluded even where it is enforced on undamaged property [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether an employee destroyed property or stole it, since destruction is outside the dishonesty exclusion and theft is not [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Whether reasonable means were used to prevent further damage after the loss, which is a separate exclusion in its own right [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
variability: This describes the 09 17 edition of the form [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17]. Endorsements add and remove exclusions and buy back perils such as earthquake, flood and ordinance or law, and the policy issued governs.
Whether a loss was caused by an excluded peril, and whether an ensuing covered peril followed, are factual determinations the form frames and does not resolve.
Specified causes of loss is a defined term at G.2 that several exceptions turn on, and this record does not set out its full contents.

The form's Section G contains only two defined terms, Fungus and Specified causes of loss; there is no defined term Water, and Volcanic Action is defined inside exclusion B.1.b rather than in the definitions [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
nextActions: Read the exclusion's final sentences before concluding a loss is uncovered, because most of these state their exception in the same paragraph [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Establish whether the loss produced a further covered peril, since that is what the ensuing-loss exceptions pay for [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Check which perils have been bought back by endorsement, particularly earthquake, flood and ordinance or law, since all three are excluded here [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Document the steps taken to prevent further damage immediately after a loss, because failing to take them is itself an exclusion [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
If fungus or rot is involved, check whether it followed a specified cause of loss and note that the Additional Coverage is capped at $15,000 in any 12-month period [S:iso-cp-10-30-09-17].
Where a denial rests on concurrent causation, take it to a lawyer rather than arguing the sequence with the adjuster.
author: Aaron Bollinger

handoff.reason: The anti-concurrent-causation lead-in means a claim can turn entirely on how the sequence of causes is characterised, which is contested on the facts and is not settled by reading the exclusion.
